QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_24

question.text: Under SAS-200, sanitation programmes can claim SROI. Which is the MOST commonly accepted monetary proxy for the OUTCOME 'averted diarrheal-disease burden'?

answer.text: Cost of treatment per diarrheal episode (WHO/public-health unit cost) × episodes averted, plus productivity-loss-day valuation
Average cost of bottled water per month
Cost of a toilet per household

explanation.text: **The Logic:** SROI monetary proxies for diarrheal disease averted use the WHO / public-health treatment-cost per episode plus productivity-loss days valued at the minimum wage. Option C toilet-cost is an input cost, not an outcome proxy; Option D GDP-per-capita is macroeconomic; Option B bottled-water is irrelevant. **The Trap:** Options B, C, D are tempting but methodologically off. Option B is tangential, Option C is input not outcome, Option D is too coarse. **Cross-Exam Context:** SROI proxy selection parallels XV (Research Analyst — DCF proxy justification) and XIX-A (AIF — valuation proxies). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When SROI assumptions matter, publish the proxy table as an annexure — reviewer challenges on SROI are 90% about the proxy choice, not the arithmetic.
